sections.title: Furniture Industry at a Crossroads: Spending Up, Sentiment Down
sections.content: The US furniture industry is showing **resilient consumer spending** despite **weakening macro signals**. Furnishings PCE reached **$507.3B in 2025** (+3.5% YoY) and quarterly spending hit a record **$533.0B in Q2 2026**, yet **consumer sentiment fell to 51.7** and **housing starts dropped to 1,275K units** — creating a tension between near-term demand strength and forward-looking risk. The global market is projected to grow from **$740B (2025) to $1.3T (2035)** at a 5.8% CAGR, but US-specific signals point to a cyclical cooldown.

data.title: Spending growth outpaces sentiment recovery
data.evidence: **Furnishings PCE hit $533.0B in Q2 2026**, up **+11.1% from $479.6B in Q1 2024**, while **consumer sentiment fell to 51.7** from a 2025 peak of 56.6. Households continue buying furniture despite weakening confidence, suggesting replacement demand and hybrid-work reconfigurations are sustaining the category.

data.title: Housing weakness threatens forward demand
data.evidence: **Housing starts dropped to 1,275K in Aug 2026** (-3.3% from Sep 2025) and **building permits fell to 1,403K**, while **homeownership slipped to 65.0%** from 65.7%. Since furniture demand correlates with housing turnover, the next 6-12 months face a structural headwind despite current spending strength.

data.title: Stock performance reveals sharp industry bifurcation
data.evidence: **Flexsteel (FLXS) returned +128.16% YTD** and **Somnigroup (SN) +58.84%**, while **La-Z-Boy (LZB) fell -18.13%** and **Leggett & Platt (LEG) -15.12%**. The divergence reflects a premium/mattress segment boom versus a traditional furniture manufacturing slump, with **FLXS RSI at 78.27 (overbought)** signaling momentum exhaustion risk.

data.title: Manufacturing earnings lag retail and building materials
data.evidence: **Furniture manufacturing earnings were $26.6B in 2024** (+2.3% YoY), trailing **building material dealers at $82.0B** (+2.6%) and **total retail trade at $939.1B** (+2.9%). Producers are capturing less of the spending growth than retailers, indicating margin compression and import competition pressure.

data.title: Global tailwinds offset domestic cyclical risk
data.evidence: The **global furniture market is projected to reach $1.3T by 2035** (5.8% CAGR) and **home office furniture alone will hit $58.6B by 2031** (7.31% CAGR). US-focused retailers face near-term cyclical pressure, but export-oriented manufacturers and home-office specialists have a structural growth runway.

sections.title: Suggested Prompts
suggested_prompts: Compare furniture manufacturing earnings vs retail trade earnings by US region for 2022-2024
Analyze housing starts impact on furnishings PCE over the next 6 months
Break down furniture stock performance by sub-segment (mattress, traditional, premium) for 2026
Explore home office furniture demand drivers and regional adoption rates
